scope: UX correction of long generation failures and command receipts in the existing shared StoryWorkspace.
behaviorReviewed: The terminal refusal identified by its own current generation error gets a business summary and optional issue count; the exact raw message and all 27 issues remain available in native collapsed details.
The primary nextAction remains server-defined and precedes the complete diagnostic in document order. Details support keyboard Enter and do not send commands.

Long unknown current errors receive a neutral summary. A later timeout does not inherit a validation label or validation issue list from an older snapshot. Short unknown errors remain visible verbatim.
The same presentation applies to the Story and Task process panels without changing the shell, confirmations, gates, controls or pending request identity.
A command acknowledgment is neutral, records receipt and does not promise future success. When polling observes failed it explicitly refers to the impediment and the next action.
Legacy technical retry still recovers its original idempotency key; the diagnostic conversation/new G1 and stale-query recovery cases remain passing.

tests.qualification: Isolated browser scenarios with simulated HTTP responses. They verify presentation, polling and controlled navigation, not an LLM correction, GitLab integration or a real DEV deployment.

limitations: Real acceptance and before/after viewport measurement remain with the parent agent on the published portal. These fixtures are not evidence that JOIASC was deployed.
There is no universal first-fold guarantee. The existing shell and context still determine how far mobile users scroll; this change removes integral diagnostics from ahead of the action.
Task full-page screenshots retain the existing sticky shell position produced by focusing the details. This review does not claim to redesign or certify that shell.
No API, agent, generated application, business data or gate was changed by this UX task. No shared real browser or publication was performed.
No metrics, targets or additional telemetry were introduced. The eight selected cases do not constitute complete system regression.
